fundamentals.summary: As of the 2026-11-06 close (USD 284.78), Alphabet shows strong y/y revenue growth (+24.7% in Q3 FY26, quarter ended 2026-09-30) and Cloud acceleration, with stable operating margin of 31.8% and debt/equity of about 0.21. Against that, y/y net income (-24.3%) and EPS (-26.1%) fell, FCF was negative for two straight quarters (USD -9.07B latest), debt rose 25.9% q/q, and capex plans are escalating. P/E inputs (trailing 14.87x, forward 18.45x) are provider-reported and distorted by volatile quarterly earnings; strong growth is offset by weak cash conversion and unverified share data, so the signal is neutral with medium confidence.

macro.fed_impact: Fed (Chair Warsh) is in a tightening bias: Sep 16 2026 FOMC raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, and Oct 28 held with a 10-2 vote in which Cook and Hammack dissented in favour of another 25bp hike. Hawkish dissents and a strong Oct jobs report (+165k vs ~65k expected, unemployment 4.1%) raise the risk of further hikes; next FOMC Dec 8-9 with a new dot plot.
macro.interest_rate_outlook: Rates are expected to stay restrictive or rise: markets priced roughly one more 25bp hike in 2026 and further hikes into 2027 (one source); Sep dot plot year-end projections 4.1%-4.4%. 10y Treasury 4.84-4.86% (Nov 5-6), 2y ~4.52%, 30y 5.26%. Higher long yields raise the cost of capital for a capex-heavy company: Alphabet Q3 capex ~$51.4B (+~114% y/y), FCF ~-$9.1B (second straight quarter capex exceeded operating cash generation), FY26 capex guide $195-205B with 2027 signalled above $300B, so funding is sensitive to borrowing costs.

Higher 10y yield (~4.85%) pressures long-duration growth valuations and the financing of AI data-center buildout

macro.summary: The dated macro snapshot is a headwind: the Fed hiked in September, held in October with two dissents favouring another hike, 10y yields sit near 4.85%, and the Nov 5 selloff cited data-center borrowing costs. Alphabet's capex ($195-205B FY26, >$300B signalled for 2027) with negative FCF makes it rate-sensitive, but Cloud growth of 103% offsets this, so macro evidence is mixed-to-negative without being decisive. Neutral with medium confidence.
